x: Four of our young milers, Clements, Chantler, Stimpson and Wood competed in an under 20 mile team race at the Enfield A.C. Open Meeting, and although our scoring men finished 4, 5, 6, we were placed second.
Edwards, of Ealing, was placed first in the match, followed by Martin, of ours, Shirley (of Ashcombe) and then Stimpson and Chantler, of ours.
George Chantler (the holder), Dave Martin, Ed Stimpson and Ken Wood were always close together; but in the closing stages Stimpson found a little extra speed to finish nine seconds ahead of Martin.
Our Junior Champion, Ted Stimpson, was in the first 10; Alec Patience and Syd Ring were lying handy in the early twenties, with the rest of ours strung out to about the eighties.

Shields did well to finish third, and among the others, Ted Stimpson was generally thought to have done well. It was pleasing to see several comparative newcomers showing fair form, which should in due course find them places in our teams.

Allum assumed second place, followed by Stimpson, but they were too far behind to make any impression on Bain. Stimpson eventually took second place, and Footer, running through the field, came into fourth place.
As is usual the cracks set the pace, Penny, Cohen (who is showing improved form this year) leading, Ring, Taylor, Stimpson and Parker being bunched just behind.
Stimpson, who was prevented from turning out by business calls. The runners were away in a pack to a slow start and kept well together until they were out of sight.
From the very start Pat Parker looked the winner and after the first mile he was leading, but followed very closely by Carter, Cohen, Stimpson and Ring, with the rest of the field in hot pursuit.
Ted Stimpson carried on in steady, long striding style, running easily. Meantime, Birchfield and Mitcham were fighting each other, and in doing so gained on our runner.
The course was altered slightly to cut out the brook but Stride's time of 29 mins. 15 secs. is, nevertheless, of the same excellent standard set by Stimpson and Clements in previous years.

As usual, they started over the circuit of the field at a cracking pace, all in a bunch with Ted Stimpson, Penny and Harry Shields leading, but by the time they were back at the start (1 mile) there were three distinct packs with six in the fast, eight in the medium and I lost count of the slow.

Jerman early cut out the pace, but Stimpson and Len Herbert raced away over the last lap of the Common. Herbert's reserve pace gave him a good win, but the form shewn by all our runners inspires confidence in their ability to win the "News of the World" event at the end of the month.
Also at this meeting was an open 3 Miles Team race, and Belgrave gained an easy win, filling first 3 places with Smart, Carter and Stimpson.
